_owner_ruling_2026_11_07.R1: Board: the OpenCV 5.1 blueprint folds into the harness/next-release graph; no second board. Its stages run as the existing NR nodes plus only new nodes or node changes that Joe merges into graph.json.
_owner_ruling_2026_11_07.R2: First GPU chain: the change-mask body in retina/t1.py (absdiff, threshold, morphological open, close), not the masked meanStdDev chain.
_owner_ruling_2026_11_07.R3: Build root: E:/OpenCV5.1_Prep (the prep project), not C:/ocv.
_owner_ruling_2026_11_07.R4: Worker runtime: CPython 3.12.10 with the isolated cp312 OpenImageIO wheel, not a hython-seeded venv and not the cp314 wheel.
_owner_ruling_2026_11_07.scope_note: R1 covers the OpenCV blueprint only. The Neural Growth (C-lane) nodes below are a proposal that needs its own owner ruling before they can enter graph.json (OD-01).

nodes.title: Build the OpenCV 5.1 CUDA artifact under the ruled E: root and lock its identity
nodes.why: No graph node owns the build (G0 receipt section 13 item 2; ADR-0002 decision 13). NR-GPU-FEASIBILITY closed B1 with a trivial non-OpenCV kernel and its predicate pins feasible-unproven, so it would go red exactly when a build succeeds (inverse gate). Under R3 the build runs under E:/OpenCV5.1_Prep, whose staged BUILD_LIST names cudaarithm and cudafilters for the R2 change-mask chain, and under R4 the binding targets CPython 3.12.10 without the limited API. The staged recipe has no install step. The receipt must record the generated (not requested) module list, both pinned source SHAs, the install step, where cv2 landed, native-file digests, OPENCV_ENABLE_NONFREE=OFF and measured durations. Waits on OD-02 (this node or a reopened FEASIBILITY), OD-12 (per-act build authorization, window, parallelism) and OD-16 (worker venv).

nodes.title: Pin the host/worker boundary: transitive zero-cv2 in-host closure, zero hou in the worker, fixed host payload
nodes.why: The zero-cv2 host lint is lexical, not transitive, no test pins zero hou in the worker, and the host installer already ships retina/t1.py, so a backend module could load CUDA into Houdini with every test green (ADR-0002 Context section 2 items 5-7). These are G0 slice 1 (G0 receipt section 11): three hermetic tests, each proven able to fail by a named mutation. If ADR-0002 is ratified they become a precondition for any backend code under retina/ (ADR-0002 section 'Consequences', item 4). Waits on OD-09 (graph home) and OD-05 (the build_payload.py allowlist coupling).

nodes.title: Make the RETINA worker runtime recipe conform to R4: CPython 3.12.10, isolated cp312 OIIO, the locked custom cv2
nodes.why: The shipped recipe documents a hython-seeded venv and names a cp314 OpenImageIO wheel, which R4 rules out, and it installs opencv-python-headless, which must never share a venv with the custom cv2 (ADR-0002 section 'Consequences of R1-R4', item 3). The three recipe files are in no node's owner_files, so they cannot change until a node owns them (G0 receipt section 5). The contract names CPython 3.12.10, the cp312 win_amd64 OIIO wheel, NumPy inside >=2,<3 and compatible with the build headers, and the build-lock receipt by digest. Waits on OD-09 (graph home) and OD-16 (worker venv location and creator; CUDA DLL resolution).

nodes.title: Add the worker-only CUDA backend for the R2 change-mask chain behind the tri-state contract
nodes.why: ADR-0002 Site 2 is a worker-only CUDA module, off the host payload list and unreachable from the in-host modules, and it is unowned. Under R2 it covers absdiff, the strict threshold, morphological open and close only. A gpu_required operation that cannot run on CUDA must yield an inconclusive check with a reason, never a silent CPU pass, and T1Unavailable must be mapped rather than raised. No backend code may land under retina/ before ADR-0002 is ratified (G0 receipt section 13 item 22). Waits on OD-11 (ratification), OD-09 (graph home) and OD-10 (cpu_reference identity).

nodes.title: Run the GPU-required profile as Joe's canary on approved non-production scenes, with disable and rollback shown
nodes.why: The OpenCV blueprint's G4 has no node (ADR-0002 Reconciliation, G4 row). It comes after demo v1 and needs a specific approval, a re-grounded runtime, render, cancel and contention probes, and an immediate disable and rollback shown with before and after evidence. Worker-package rollback is unavailable until NR-WORKER-SUPERVISED and NR-PACKAGE-PAIR exist. Waits on OD-12 (what demo v1 means; resource window) and OD-21 (canary before or after packaging).

nodes.title: Prove native H22 neural cellular automata growth in one manually controlled, disposable sandbox
nodes.why: Neural Growth C1. The Core, Decode and training node types exist on 22.0.400 and 22.0.466 by a fenced parameter probe that created and cooked nothing, so cook, model load and provider choice are UNKNOWN. SYNAPSE has no in-process sandbox; the only isolation precedent is a separate session with a cleared, never-saved scene. The receipt must show matched Core/Decode model hashes, a declared decode colour transform, fixed-seed replay within a tolerance frozen beforehand, an extended rollout, stop and restart results, the executing provider and a sandbox-only scene path. It does not certify the OpenCV lane and carries no edge from the GPU nodes (Neural Growth blueprint section 10). Waits on OD-01 (C-lane adoption) and OD-18 (Houdini launch, build choice, resource window).

nodes.title: Turn reference evidence into a versioned control package with explicit units, domains and coordinates
nodes.why: Neural Growth C2. RETINA today measures and emits verdicts; producing control fields that steer synthesis is a new allocation, so it needs a ratified amendment for reference-driven control generation, separate from ADR-0002's CUDA backend. The contract names who produced each field and how, how confident it is, its shape and value domain, what each channel means, its coordinate frame and a digest per field; it maps rotation to turns and respects the documented 0.2-1 scale clamp, and rejects malformed input. Its native mapping is pinned to the committed NCA sandbox receipt, so NR-VG-NCA-SANDBOX is a dep, not optional evidence. A CPU-reference first slice needs no GPU edge; the GPU path reads NR-GPU-QUALIFICATION. Waits on OD-01, OD-19 (the amendment; CPU-first or GPU path) and OD-10.

nodes.title: Expose Grow as one bounded, cancellable sandbox preview job with stale-output rejection and no scene writes
nodes.why: Neural Growth C3. The four existing COP growth tools build nodes inside the open scene and the autonomous worker may call them with no prompt, and the worker is denied a preview render by policy, so a Grow job cannot reuse that path without breaking the no-production-write criterion. It needs a separate-process sandbox, atomic publication (products, manifest, completion marker last), stale-marker rejection, resource admission and a real Stop. Registering it needs python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py and the panel executor files, which NR-SPARSE-RENDER and NR-WRITE-RECEIPT own; this node takes none of them (OD-06). Waits on OD-01, OD-06 and OD-18.

nodes.title: Close the creative loop: comparison and refinement in a creative sidecar kept separate from verdicts
nodes.why: Neural Growth C4. Creative ranking must live in a separate versioned sidecar linked to the perception verdicts; it never extends the envelope {ch, v, tier, claim, checks, verdict, proof, at} or the tri-state roll-up, a style score never overrides a failed protection or provenance check, and an empty mandatory-check list never satisfies a creative job. Joe's review against reference-only and guided baselines is the acceptance. Waits on OD-01.

nodes.title: Qualify Keep as a reviewed promotion proposal: exact target, explicit approval, recovery rehearsed
nodes.why: Neural Growth C5. Keep stores a candidate in the sandbox and prepares a proposal; applying it to a working scene is a separate, explicitly authorized act. Undo grouping is not rollback, so the proposal carries an exact-target diff, the original state, the approval scope and a rehearsed recovery, and it mutates only through the authored-write receipt path. autonomy/planner.py, driver.py and models.py stay with NR-PLAN-TRUTH. Waits on OD-01 and per-act approval of every scene change.

_proposed_changes_to_existing.current: Source support, a built module, an executed call and a release-qualified operation are four different states. The blueprint's hand-computable fixtures (neutral RGB ramps, the 11x11 census, signed HDR, NaN/Inf counts, equality at the FP32 threshold) and the backend witness are what turn the second state into the fourth.
_proposed_changes_to_existing.proposed: Source support, a built module, an executed call and a release-qualified operation are four different states. Owner ruling 2026-11-07: the first GPU chain to qualify is the change-mask body in retina/t1.py - absdiff, threshold, morphological open and close (R2) - on the artifact built under E:/OpenCV5.1_Prep (R3), not C:/ocv. Not ruled, and left to Joe: whether the masked meanStdDev census and its hand-computable fixtures (neutral RGB ramps, the 11x11 census, signed HDR, NaN/Inf counts, equality at the FP32 threshold) are replaced by this chain or kept as an additional chain (ADR-0002 decision 14, OD-22); the cpu_reference identity (OD-10); and this node's gate (OD-23). G0-proposed, not ruled (G0 receipt slice 2; report 02-ops section 7): the change-mask fixtures (changes at frame edges and corners; |diff| at and one float32 ulp either side of diff_threshold; non-contiguous and odd-stride arrays; sizes not multiples of 16 or 32; an empty change set) and identical mask bytes as the parity criterion. INFERENCE: a NaN in a luma plane is a CPU-versus-CUDA threshold-parity hazard, so the draft predicate also asks for a NaN fixture. The backend witness and a per-operation dispatch record still turn the second state into the fourth.

_proposed_changes_to_existing.note: The current predicate is an existence gate that an empty file satisfies. The replacement test does not exist in the repo; its full draft is carried below in proposed_file and must be written to proposed_file.path in the same commit as Joe's merge of this change, or the predicate is red for the wrong reason (file not found). validate_amendment.py writes the draft to a temporary folder and runs it: it is red today for its declared marker (no committed qualification receipt). Its cpu_reference assertion waits on OD-10 and its location inside the K1-shared harness/next-release/gpu/ waits on OD-04. Because those are owner decisions and the node's gate is crux, OD-23 asks Joe to move the gate to joe or strike the Joe-ruled assertion.

_owner_decisions.question: Adopt the Neural Growth C-lane into the next-release graph at all, and widen the graph objective to include a creative loop. R1 rules the OpenCV blueprint only; the G0 receipt lists the Neural Growth blueprint as not reconciled.

Who owns the build: this new NR-VG-GPU-BUILD-LOCK node, or NR-GPU-FEASIBILITY reopened as a round-three build lock with a replaced predicate (its current test pins feasible-unproven). ADR-0002 decision 13.

K4: NR-FOLLOW-ON owns all of harness/next-release/, including graph.json, both rulings, the README and this proposals/ folder with its predicate files. Narrow it (for example to harness/next-release/follow_on/ and follow_on_done.json) or leave the predicates unowned. New receipts are placed under harness/vision/ so that no new node collides with it.
K1: NR-GPU-FEASIBILITY and NR-GPU-QUALIFICATION both own harness/next-release/gpu/, where the proposed qualification test would live.

K2 and the payload coupling: installer/build_payload.py is owned twice, and the proposed payload-exclusion guard reads it, so any intended payload change must update the guard's allowlist in the same commit.

K3/K6: registering a Grow tool needs python/synapse/mcp/_tool_registry.py (NR-SPARSE-RENDER and NR-WRITE-RECEIPT) and the panel executor files (NR-WRITE-RECEIPT); adding a registry tool also moves the tool-count pins in CLAUDE.md and the README. Which node makes those edits.
K5: widen NR-IMAGE-CONTRACT to own the retina/t1.py backend seam, or sequence the seam as its own node, and order it against the Y change (ADR-0002 decisions 12b and 15).
